title: optimize-evals-1on1-prep-2026-03-04
content:
Purpose: prep for 1:1 with Samir (review recent eval run + A/B results). Quick notes, unanswered questions, and action items I want to align on.

Background/context:
- Last week we rolled the new prompt set (prompt-v2) to 10% traffic for hosted chat endpoints as a canary.
- Eval harness (eval-run-2026-03-02) shows a subtle but consistent quality regression on the customer-NLU set: -2.3% exact-match / -1.8% BLEU relative to baseline prompt-v1.
- A/B experiment (AB-2026-03-02) shows latency and cost unchanged, but hallucination-rate proxy (entity-fabrication metric) increased from 3.2% -> 5.0% on canary traffic.
- Observability: token-level cost and latency dashboards look stable. Per-route error traces show a bump in short-context failures (~<64 tokens) that correlate with a few specific prompts.

Things to cover in 1:1:
1) Quick recap (2 min) — share top-line numbers and where the regression is concentrated.
2) Fail-mode analysis (8 min) — examples, patterns, and whether this is prompt ordering, system message change, or edge-case formatting.
3) Rollout decision (5 min) — hold/rollback vs expand with mitigations.
4) Action plan + owners (5 min) — who does what and timelines.

Initial hypotheses (what to validate):
- Hypothesis A: prompt-v2 introduced a subtle system-message phrasing change that reduces model grounding for entity extraction prompts. Check diff between system messages in prompt-v1 vs v2.
- Hypothesis B: prompt-v2 is longer on avg and pushes more requests into different attention kernel path—possible tokenization differences leading to hallucination on short contexts. Need seq-length distribution and kernel path logs.
- Hypothesis C: dataset bias — the NLU eval set has a particular template that interacts poorly with the new few-shot examples we added. Run ablations removing the new examples.

Immediate data pulls I want before/after the call (would be great if Samir can grab these):
- Top 20 failing prompts from eval-run-2026-03-02 with full model responses (redaction OK).
- Distribution of sequence lengths for canary vs baseline traffic last 72h.
- Kernel selection / execution path breakdown for requests hitting canary vs baseline (if available from serving logs).
- Confusion matrix / per-intent F1 deltas for the customer-NLU set.

Notes on examples (copying a couple of sketch failures for discussion):
- Example A: user asks for slot extraction; model invents an extra location field not present in text. (likely hallucination)
- Example B: short utterance (~12 tokens) returns a generic fallback instead of the expected intent classification.

Potential mitigations to propose:
- Immediate: pause canary expansion and revert prompt-v2 to prompt-v1 for 100% of traffic (fast rollback).
- Short-term (1–3 days): run ablation (remove new few-shot examples) and test whether hallucination drops.
- Medium-term (1–2 weeks): add constrained decoding tweaks (e.g., ban-list for entity types?) and extend eval harness with targeted probes for the failing templates.
- Product/UX mitigation: if rollback is too risky, throttle canary bandwidth and add fallback policy to route failing prompts to a more conservative model variant.

Action items (draft):
- Olivia: Compile top-20 failing examples and attach to ticket JIRA-OPT-1234 by EOD 2026-03-04.
- Samir: Pull kernel-exec-path logs + seq-length distribution and post to Slack thread #optimize-evals by 2026-03-04 5pm PT.
- Jamie: Run ablation removing new few-shot examples on eval harness (eval-run-ablate-1) and share metrics by 2026-03-05.
- Eng (TBD): Prepare rollback plan for multi-region canary (estimate ~30 min ops) — assign in incident runbook if we decide to rollback.

Questions for Samir (to ask):
- Do we have any recent infra changes (compiler/kernel upgrades) that coincided with the prompt-v2 rollout?
- Any other experiments running on same endpoints that could confound the A/B (e.g., quantization profile change, caching enabled)?
- Is it feasible to quickly route 100% of failing traffic to a more conservative model variant in the control plane?

Risk assessment and recommended default:
- Regression magnitude is moderate (-2.3% EM on a focused set) but concentrated on high-value NLU templates; hallucination increase is more concerning for customer trust. Recommended default: pause expansion, target ablation + quick rollback if ablation doesn't show >1.5% recovery.

Misc notes / links:
- Eval harness job: eval-run-2026-03-02 (see dashboard link above).
- Current canary config: prompt-v2 @ 10% traffic, model variant: redwood-7b-q4f16, decoding: default (top-p 0.9).
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/876 (prompt changes).

Tone for 1:1: concise + action-oriented. Want alignment on whether to pause and who executes rollback. Also want decision criterion: if ablation recovers >=1.5% EM by EOD 2026-03-05 then we can proceed to a slow expansion to 25% with monitoring; otherwise rollback to prompt-v1 and open a small investigation sprint.

Follow-up (post 1:1): I will update this doc with final decision and move to JIRA ticket notes.

End of prep notes.
